headline: Sales and profit climb as margins hold steady
summary_short: AWI's Q2 2026 revenue rose 11.2% y/y to $472M on higher volumes, favorable pricing and recent acquisitions, while net income climbed 10.1% to $96.7M and diluted EPS rose 12.4% to $2.26.
summary_long: Net sales grew 11.2% y/y to $472M on higher Mineral Fiber AUV and volumes plus Architectural Specialties organic growth and the Eventscape, Parallel and Geometrik acquisitions. Cost of goods sold ticked up to 58.7% of sales (58.6% prior year) as acquisition costs offset AUV gains, tariff refunds and manufacturing productivity; SG&A rose on incentive compensation and growth investment. WAVE equity earnings rose to $33.6M. Operating income rose 8.6% y/y to $133.8M, net income rose 10.1% to $96.7M, and diluted EPS rose 12.4% to $2.26 as the diluted share count fell on buybacks. AWI repurchased $74.9M of stock, paid a $0.339/share quarterly dividend, and ended the quarter with $78.6M of cash. No forward guidance was disclosed in the filing.

drivers.explanation: Sales and profit both grew on higher volumes, favorable average unit value and recent bolt-on acquisitions, while cost ratios held roughly flat despite input-cost inflation and tariff impacts.
Growth came from $31M of higher volumes (organic Architectural Specialties growth, the Eventscape/Parallel/Geometrik acquisitions, and Mineral Fiber volume) plus $16M of favorable average unit value.
COGS ticked up to 58.7% of sales from 58.6% as the 2026/2025 acquisitions added cost, partly offset by favorable AUV, manufacturing productivity and $2M of IEEPA tariff refunds.
Both segments grew gross profit as favorable AUV and higher volumes outpaced manufacturing, freight and energy cost inflation and the acquisitions' added cost base.
Higher gross profit was partly offset by SG&A growth from incentive compensation, selling investment and inorganic acquisition costs.
Moves in line with GAAP operating income this quarter; the two metrics sit within $1M of each other.
EBITDA growth outpaced EBIT as quarterly depreciation and amortization ($30.2M) was little changed from a year ago, so most of the EBIT gain flowed through to EBITDA.
Benefited from higher operating income, higher WAVE equity earnings ($33.6M vs $32.1M) and lower interest expense on reduced rates and average debt.
Tracked the pretax income gain; the effective tax rate was little changed at 23.8% versus 23.9% a year ago.
Per-share growth outpaced net income growth as the diluted share count fell about 2% y/y on the ongoing buyback program.
First-half operating cash flow of $125.9M was more than absorbed by the Eventscape acquisition, capex, buybacks and dividends, per the filing's cash-flow discussion.
Not explained in the release as a standalone quarterly move.
The quarterly dip is consistent with $74.9M of share buybacks and roughly $14M of dividends paid, partly offset by retained net income.
AWI repurchased 0.5 million shares in the quarter (0.8 million over the first half) under its ongoing share-repurchase program.
